description: Baseline is launch-overhead-bound: ~74k tiny kernel launches are 91% of time on B=640 n=512. Write a single fused Triton kernel that factors the whole batch in one launch — one program per matrix loads A into SRAM and runs unblocked Householder QR column-by-column (column norm to reflector v,tau, then rank-1 trailing update A-=v*(tau*(v^T A))) in SRAM/registers, writing compact H (R in upper triangle, v below diagonal) and tau in torch.geqrf convention. Scope to SRAM-resident n (32,176; tile 352 if feasible). Route off-grid n and shapes too large for SRAM to torch.geqrf.

Baseline runs SIMT sgemm (no tensor cores) on the dominant n=512(B=640)/1024(B=60) shapes. Implement blocked compact-WY Householder QR in Triton: factor width-b≈32-64 column panels with unblocked Householder (FP32), build the triangular T factor, then apply the block reflector (I-V T V^T) to the trailing submatrix as batched tl.dot GEMMs on TF32 tensor cores with FP32 accumulation. Keep panel and T-factor in FP32 to hold orthogonality. Emit geqrf-convention H,tau. Route off-grid n to torch.geqrf. Target compute throughput and launch overhead on the large shapes.

Leaderboard leaders hit ~1300µs via low-bit (mxfp10/mxfp4); the task permits low-bit internally if FP32 factors pass the gates. Build a mixed-precision blocked Householder QR for the large shapes (n=512/1024/2048): trailing-update block-reflector GEMMs in BF16 (then explore FP8) on tensor cores with FP32 accumulation, keeping panel factorization in FP32 and recomputing reflectors/tau in FP32 from corrected panels so the emitted compact-H is genuine. Hold the 20*n*eps factor tolerance with a FIXED-iteration correction (no data-dependent stopping — invariance guard). Emit FP32 geqrf-convention H,tau. Off-grid n to torch.geqrf.

n=352 (B=40) is still on geqrf at 38,616us and is an equally-weighted geomean shape nobody covers; your monolithic n=352 spilled, but a BLOCKED panel fits. Extend your fused single-launch kernel with a blocked-WY Householder path for n=352: one CTA per matrix, process width-b≈32 column panels staging only rows×b in SMEM (352×32×4≈45KB), factor each panel with your unblocked Householder, build the larft T-factor, apply the block reflector (I−V T V^T) to the trailing columns, advancing across panels. Worker 1's working n=512 panel kernel (branch worker-1-brief-0, commit 8c58bcc) is a direct template. Keep n=32/176 on your fused path; route n≥512 to geqrf. Emit exact geqrf-convention H,tau; pass all guards.

Your key finding stands: the FP32 panel is the lever, low-bit is capped/inaccurate. Worker 1's single-CTA Triton panel already won n=176-1024 (global best 12,594us, 9.3x). The two UNOWNED equally-weighted shapes are the large-n tail still on geqrf: n=2048 (B=8, 74,912us) and n=4096 (B=2, 50,471us). These are NOT batch-parallel (8 and 2 matrices) so one-CTA-per-matrix starves the GPU — occupancy must come from TILING WITHIN each matrix across many CTAs. Build a multi-CTA blocked-WY Householder QR for n=2048/4096: a grid of CTAs cooperating on each large matrix's panel factorization + tensor-core trailing update, keeping panel/T-factor FP32. Start from W1's panel kernel (parent commit b959d78) as your template for n=176-1024 and ADD the large-n path; keep all of W1's wins. Off-grid n to geqrf; pass all guards.

The FP32 panel factorization is the latency wall (8% occupancy, sequential Householder chains) on the dominant high-batch n=512(B=640)/1024 shapes. Replace it with a CholeskyQR2 panel: Gram G=A^T A (tensor-core GEMM), Cholesky G=R^T R, Q=A R^-1 (triangular solve), reconstruct compact reflectors+tau via orhr_col — all high-occupancy GEMMs, no per-column chain. Use 2-pass shifted CholeskyQR2. PRIMARY DESIGN: per-SHAPE fallback to the existing blocked-WY panel (never per-matrix — invariance guard) for any shape that fails the gate; run an up-front per-shape validation sweep. The BINDING constraint on rankdef/nearrank/clustered/mixed is Q-orthogonality (100*n*eps), report worst factor AND worst orth residual per shape. Branch keeps the blocked-WY path as fallback; reuse W2's orhr_col code (commit a4d9c3ea). Off-grid n to geqrf.

Combine the two best lineages into one kernel that wins every shape. Parent 1 (W1 global best c6d5097c, 7704us) has the fastest n=176/352/512/1024 blocked-WY panel (in-place strided H, fused T^T, num_warps tuning) but only a row-tiled n=2048 (44ms) and cuSOLVER n=4096. Parent 2 (your branch 2ce5b7fb, 10527us) has the CholeskyQR+orhr_col n=2048 panel (31.6ms, 2.37x — beats parent 1's 44ms) plus your TF32-trailing n=4096. Integrate: take parent 1's n<=1024 paths verbatim, graft your CholeskyQR n=2048 and TF32 n=4096 paths on top, so the merged kernel uses each lineage's best path per shape. Expect geomean below 7704us. Keep all per-shape fallbacks; pass all guards; emit exact geqrf H,tau.

Your panel is latency/reduction-bound at 8% occupancy on the dominant n=512(B=640)/1024 shapes — the cost is launch latency + HBM round-trips as the panel transits between the factor kernel and the trailing-GEMM kernel, NOT FLOPs. Build a persistent per-matrix MEGAKERNEL: one launch keeps the width-b panel resident in SMEM/registers across the whole factor->build-T->trailing-update->advance loop, collapsing per-panel launches and HBM traffic. Use recursive/blocked-WY tl.dot GEMMs as the trailing-update CONTENT for tensor-core arithmetic intensity (note: this blocks the trailing update, it does NOT shorten the sequential panel column chain — don't chase an O(log b) critical-path win that the data dependency forbids). Pure Householder throughout = unconditionally stable (no kappa^2 risk), so this also speeds the fallback path the ill-conditioned shapes need. Emit exact geqrf H,tau; off-grid n to geqrf; pass all guards.

n=4096 (B=2) is now the single slowest shape (~47ms) and dominates the geomean. PROFILE IT FIRST to split panel vs trailing-update time: for a square 4096x4096 right-looking blocked QR the trailing GEMM is the majority of flops/time and the panel is over-represented only because it's latency-bound. Attack the dominant term: right-looking blocked QR with a LARGE block size (b=128/256 to cut the number of serial panel steps) and the trailing (I-V T V^T) update as big TF32 tensor-core cuBLAS GEMMs that already fill the GPU at n=4096. Only if profiling shows the panel still dominates, accelerate it with a recursive (Elmroth-Gustavson) or TSQR panel; a cooperative-grid multi-CTA panel is a LAST resort. DO NOT use CUDA streams (validate.sh bans any 'stream' reference - leaderboard DQ). Keep all other shapes on global-best paths; emit exact geqrf H,tau; off-grid n to geqrf; pass all guards.

The two best branches are complementary, not ordered — stack them. Parent 1 (your dd598df8, 6149us) has the restored fused n=32 kernel (18.5us, the combine lineage had silently dropped it back to geqrf 291us) on top of W1's n=176-1024 panel, but only the OLD n=2048 (row-tiled 44ms) and n=4096 (cuSOLVER) paths. Parent 2 (W2 combine a55db107, 6928us) has the CholeskyQR n=2048 panel (31.6ms) and torch-TF32 n=4096 trailing (47ms) but DROPPED your n=32 kernel. Integrate so EVERY shape uses its best path: your n=32 + W1's n=176-1024 + W2's CholeskyQR n=2048 + W2's TF32 n=4096. This strands ~780us of already-won per-shape gains into one kernel. Verify each shape's choice by per-shape timing; pass all guards; emit exact geqrf H,tau.

Your megakernel result proved the dominant n=512(B640)/1024(B60) panel is compute/parallelism-bound (3.4 waves, well-occupied), NOT launch/HBM-bound — and its cost is the flat unblocked-Householder column loop doing serial SIMT rank-1 reductions. Attack THAT: replace the flat panel with a RECURSIVE/sub-blocked WY panel (LAPACK geqrt3 / Elmroth-Gustavson). Split the width-b panel into sub-panels of width b/2 (or b/4), factor each, and apply the intra-panel trailing update between sub-panels as small tl.dot tensor-core GEMMs (W=T2^T(V2^T C), C-=V2 W) instead of rank-1 SIMT ops — converting the panel's internal serial reductions into tensor-core work. Pure Householder = unconditionally stable. Branch off the current global best dd598df8 (has your panel + restored n=32). Keep n outside 512/1024 on existing paths; emit exact geqrf H,tau; pass all guards.

n=512 (4 shapes) + n=1024 (3 shapes) are 7 of 12 geomean terms — the dominant region. W1 is on their PANEL (recursive); you take their TRAILING-update GEMM, currently a uniform tf32x3 (3 passes for accuracy). W2 established orthogonality is immune to trailing precision (it depends only on the FP32 panel reflectors), and only the FACTOR residual needs the extra passes — and only near the diagonal where R's large entries sit. Try a DIAGONAL-DISTANCE-AWARE precision schedule for the (I-V T V^T) trailing update: tf32x3 on trailing column-blocks near the just-factored panel (where R-error feeds the factor gate), cheaper plain-tf32 (1 pass, ~3x faster) on far trailing blocks whose contribution to the gated leading R entries is negligible. W1 found GLOBAL mixed precision overshoots the n=512 factor gate (24-30 vs 20) — a position-aware schedule is the untried refinement. Validate the gate per-shape incl. the ill-conditioned n=512 rankdef/clustered/mixed. Branch off global best d0f4a341; emit exact geqrf H,tau; pass all guards.

The leaderboard #1 (~1317us B200) is ~4x our 5550us — a structural gap. n=512 (B=640) is 4 of 12 geomean terms and the proving ground. Its one-CTA-per-matrix Triton panel sits at 16.5% occupancy / 41.8% compute: the panel's serial BLAS-2 column reduction can't fill an SM, and the fix is hiding that latency behind OTHER matrices (you proved more-SMs-per-matrix fails: grid.sync 3x slower). Write a raw-CUDA PERSISTENT kernel for n=512 that keeps the panel resident in SMEM/registers and runs MULTIPLE matrices in flight per CTA with WARP-SPECIALIZATION (producer warps factor a panel while consumer warps apply the prior panel's tf32x3 tensor-core trailing update) — interleaving independent matrices' stalls to raise occupancy and tensor-core utilization, no HBM round-trip between panel and trailing. FIRST: ncu the current n=512 path for tensor-pipe-active % to confirm the headroom. Start from the structure; escalate to hand-written mma/wgmma only if profiling justifies. Build against stock CUB/Thrust, NO streams, per-SHAPE not per-matrix. Emit exact geqrf H,tau; keep other shapes on global-best paths; pass all guards.

Your own finding: the n=512/1024 trailing update is DRAM-bandwidth-bound (88% DRAM, ~16% compute), and the lever is reducing DRAM TRAFFIC. The current kernel is RIGHT-LOOKING: every panel immediately writes the entire trailing submatrix, so each column is read+written ~n/bw times across the factorization — maximal traffic. Reformulate as LEFT-LOOKING blocked Householder: defer updates so a column-block is touched only just before it's factored — apply all prior reflectors to that block in one fused pass (one read + one write per block instead of n/bw), then factor it. Same reflectors, same compact-H output (numerically identical, pure Householder, no accuracy change), but a large cut in trailing DRAM write traffic — the exact bottleneck you measured. Target n=512 (4 shapes) and n=1024 (3 shapes), the dominant 7/12. This is an ALGORITHMIC restructure of the factorization loop, distinct from W2's persistent-kernel implementation and W1's panel recursion. Branch off b6dd1d83; emit exact geqrf H,tau; keep small shapes + n>=2048 on existing paths; pass all guards.

You proved left-looking cuts n=512/1024 trailing DRAM traffic to 0.333x and is numerically correct, but Triton can't hold the full-height resident block (200KB > 101KB SMEM). The fix is a register+SMEM-resident persistent kernel in raw CUDA — build it, but for n=1024 (B=60), leaving n=512 (B=640) to W2 so the two dominant regions are attacked in parallel. n=1024 is a DISTINCT regime: 2x-taller panel (1024 rows), 10x fewer matrices (B=60, less batch to hide panel latency), bw=16 — so its tiling/occupancy differs from n=512 and needs its own kernel. Use load_inline raw CUDA: stream the [1024,bw] column block through registers across reflector applications (left-looking, one read+write per block), warp-specialized panel-factor vs tensor-core trailing, no HBM round-trip. Reuse your validated left-looking Householder math + geqrf-convention output. Build against stock CUB/Thrust, NO streams, per-SHAPE. Branch off fb178836; keep other shapes on global-best paths; emit exact geqrf H,tau; pass all guards incl n=1024 nearrank.

Three Triton attacks on the n=512/1024 PANEL have now failed (your megakernel, W0 CholeskyQR2, your recursive-WY) — the flat panel is the Triton floor. But the TRAILING update is ~60% of n=512 and W0 proved it's DRAM-bandwidth-bound, with a validated left-looking reformulation that cuts traffic to 0.333x (just SMEM-infeasible in Triton). Attack the n=512 TRAILING (distinct from W2's n=512 PANEL kernel and W0's n=1024): build a raw-CUDA left-looking trailing kernel streaming the [512,bw] block through registers (one read+write/block), seeded with W0's already-validated left-looking Householder math (commit fb178836, n=64 passes fr=5/orth=54 eps). PRE-VALIDATED FALLBACK if raw-CUDA stalls past ~25min: reformulate the panel's per-column rank-1 reductions as pure-PyTorch BATCHED strided cuBLAS GEMMs over all 640 matrices at once (batch as the primary parallelism dim) — zero custom CUDA, cannot fail to compile, pure Householder. Do NOT use cooperative grid-sync (proven 3x slower) or CUDA streams (banned). Branch off b6dd1d83; emit exact geqrf H,tau; pass all guards.

FP8 is the one untried dominant-shape lever (sm_120 supports _scaled_mm FP8; leaders use mxfp). TIME-BOXED FALSIFICATION (~30-40min, then fold): try a 3xFP8 error-corrected trailing-update (C-=V T V^T) ONLY on the well-conditioned n=512 seed-1029 shape, panel stays FP32. KILL-CRITERIA (must meet BOTH or revert): beat the current tf32x3 trailing on wallclock AND pass the factor gate <=1.22e-3. STRONG PRIOR IT FAILS: the trailing is DRAM-bandwidth-bound (not compute) so FP8's compute win is irrelevant unless C is STORED in FP8 (which breaks the gate); and 3xFP8 to reach 2^-10 accuracy is ~as much work as 1 tf32x3 pass. If it doesn't beat tf32x3 on wallclock within the time box, log the clean negative and stop — do NOT grind. A measured FP8 negative closes the last open lever. Branch off 4e1eaa6509555c5da91856d10ae4be10b897ad68; emit exact geqrf H,tau; pass all guards.
